items.excerpt: Announced at OpenAI DevDay 2026: Adobe's ChatGPT plugin gains interactive, hands-on editors for images, designs and PDFs, powered by Photoshop and Adobe Express, so users can describe an edit in chat and then fine-tune it by hand in the panel. (page gives date only: 09-29-2026)

OpenAI is expanding ChatGPT plugins with dedicated sidebar surfaces, app-like interfaces and automations; Canva, Figma and Adobe are among the named early examples of apps that render UI inside ChatGPT.
OpenAI is expanding Codex with reusable cloud development environments that persist across devices, which lowers setup friction for prompt-to-app and vibe-coding workflows.
An essay arguing that vibe coding isn't the problem; the missing half is the specification, design and engineering thinking that has to happen before an AI agent starts building.

Anthropic released Claude Sonnet 5.5 (Sept 28, 2026): 30%+ faster and up to 30% cheaper than Sonnet 5. It is strongest on everyday tasks and polished documents, slides and spreadsheets, and Anthropic says it has 'a sharp eye for design'. (page gives date only)

Runway joins the OpenAI Marketplace as a launch partner. Enterprise teams can now purchase the best from Runway and other labs into one workspace, including Gen-4.5, Seedance 2.5, GPT Image 2.5 and ElevenLabs V4.
The French beverage company’s 15-person creative pod turns one ad script into several animated styles in Runway, testing which one wins on Meta within days.

Animators Guillermo Miranda and Javier de la Chica explain what making an 11-minute animated Don Quixote short with AI actually involved: the roles people still had to fill, the risks, and where generative tools hit serious creative limits.
The Verge's roundup of OpenAI DevDay 2026 covers GPT-6.1 Sol, dots agents, ChatGPT plugins with app-like UI, Codex updates and new builder tools.
OpenAI launched dots, always-on personal agents that each have their own visual character. Users will soon be able to run several of them at once.

A design read on OpenAI's new dots agents: instead of the void logo, each dot gets a cute, blobby character design (a triangle with a bow tie, a bunny and others), a deliberate branding shift for agentic AI. (date/body from the FC RSS feed; site returns 403)

Epoch AI's Furniture Assembly Benchmark uses Ikea instruction manuals to test AI models' spatial reasoning. Even top models still can't reliably assemble the furniture. (date/body from the FC RSS feed)

AgiBot has released 300+ autonomous, mostly humanoid robots into Chimelong Spaceship Park in Zhuhai, where they roam freely among visitors. It's the largest public embodied-AI deployment yet and a live test of how robot design meets people. (date/body from the FC RSS feed)

Tips for anyone who vibecodes: people can spot and dislike AI slop but don't know how to fix it. This piece gives designers concrete ways to de-slopify AI-generated interfaces. (date/body from the Medium RSS feed; site is Cloudflare-walled)

From specialist makers to strategic orchestrators: the piece argues that when AI compresses execution time, demand for design vision and systems thinking goes up, which is the Jevons paradox applied to design. (RSS has a teaser only)
Artists Xin Liu and Eunjo Lee used Google AI to create new artworks with LAS Art Foundation and Google Arts & Culture Lab.
Google Arts & Culture turns 15 with an app redesign: visual-first conversational search, a redesigned home feed, AI experiments and 27 new city guides.
Meta's Muse AI agent is coming to its smart glasses "soon", letting it take actions at your request while your phone stays in your pocket.

Meta Ray-Ban Display launches in the UK and Canada and gets new features, including AI-driven 'Hologram' avatars for WhatsApp video calls (set up from a face scan plus sample speech) and Meta AI calendar access.
Liminal is taking its wellness approach outside the headset. Liminal: Walking Meditation uses Meta AI glasses to create a spoken meditation around what you actually see.
Hands-on with Meta's 'Hologram' avatars from Connect: voice-driven, AI-infused 2.5D photoreal avatars that Meta positions against Apple Personas for its VR and display glasses.
